facts.fact: Q2 2026 revenue was $1.898 billion; the company reported 26% year-over-year growth.
Q2 2026 GAAP diluted EPS was $0.70, versus $0.22 in Q2 2025.
Company guidance for Q3 2026 GAAP diluted EPS was $0.72-$0.82.
Company guidance for 2026 capital expenditure was $2.5-$3.0 billion.
Communications, including smartphones and tablets, represented 42% of Q2 2026 revenue.
Computing represented 22% of Q2 2026 revenue; the category includes data centers, infrastructure, PCs/laptops and storage, and is not disclosed AI-only revenue.

Amkor announced a $1.5 billion multi-year advanced packaging and development agreement with NVIDIA. NVIDIA will provide a prepayment supporting U.S. capacity expansion; the announced amount is not recognized quarterly revenue.
Amkor increased planned total Arizona campus investment to approximately $12 billion.
Arizona phase 2 construction is planned to begin in late 2027, with completion expected by the end of 2029.
Q2 2026 revenue was $258.2 million, up 31.9% year over year.
Q2 2026 GAAP diluted EPS was $0.71, versus $0.12 a year earlier.
Q2 2026 company-defined free cash flow was $52.6 million.
FormFactor reported HBM and co-packaged optics demand contributed to sequential increases in Probe Cards and Systems revenue, respectively.
Company guidance for Q3 2026 GAAP diluted EPS was $0.75 plus or minus $0.09.
Q2 2026 revenue was $343.1 million, up 35.3% year over year.
Q2 2026 GAAP diluted EPS was $1.21, versus $0.69 a year earlier.
Q2 2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS was $1.93, versus $1.25 a year earlier.
Management reported backlog exceeding $1 billion for the first time. Backlog is not recognized revenue.
Company guidance for Q3 2026 GAAP diluted EPS was $1.54-$1.70.
The balance sheet reported $1.471731 billion of 2031 notes, net; cash holdings must not be described as equivalent net cash.
Q2 2026 revenue was $133.2 million, with company-reported year-over-year growth of 8%.
Q2 2026 GAAP net income was $23.3 million, down 31% year over year.
Company guidance for Q3 2026 revenue was $158-$160 million.
Management reported year-to-date order intake over $600 million, with delivery scheduled across the remainder of 2026 and into 2027.
Fiscal 2026 revenue was $50.0 million, versus $59.0 million in fiscal 2025.
Company guidance for the fiscal year ending June 25, 2027 was revenue of $130-$150 million; this is a forecast, not realized sales.
Aehr announced a $22 million follow-on AI processor wafer-level burn-in production order from its lead customer; shipment was expected over the next six months.

quote_note: Latest provider quotes, not verified regular-session closes; quote dates in U.S. Eastern time are 2026-09-18. Provider P/E basis has not been independently reconstructed.
calculation_caveats: Quarterly EPS annualization is a sensitivity illustration only. It is not trailing P/E, consensus forward P/E, a full-year earnings forecast or a price target; it assumes one quarter repeats four times.
AEHR calculation is equity market capitalization/sales, not EV/sales. Forecast revenue is not guaranteed.
Different business models, margins, capital intensity and growth require different valuation multiples; a lower multiple alone is not evidence of mispricing.

assessments.thesis: Price/growth balance candidate. Existing earnings recovery plus contracted advanced-packaging capacity create a stronger case than a distant factory story alone.
assessments.bear: Low-margin capital-intensive OSAT, substantial non-AI exposure, execution/funding/FCF risk. Partnership value and customer prepayment are not current revenue.
next_checks: Q3 EPS and gross margin delivery
Computing/AI mix and repeat customer orders
Capital expenditure, customer prepayments and free cash flow reconciliation
downgrade_conditions: Funding needs rise faster than contracted profitable demand
Major customer or Arizona execution deteriorates

assessments.thesis: Current HBM/probe-card and optical-test demand is already supported by GAAP earnings and free cash flow.
assessments.bear: Valuation assumes sustained growth and margins; memory/test cycles and customer spending can reverse. Do not treat all company sales as AI.
next_checks: Persistence of gross margins and cash conversion
HBM and optical test customer concentration and competitive positioning
downgrade_conditions: HBM or optical test demand weakens
Gross margins or cash conversion deteriorate structurally

assessments.thesis: Process control exposure across advanced logic, HBM and packaging plus record backlog provides multiple growth drivers.
assessments.bear: Large GAAP/non-GAAP earnings gap, valuation risk, backlog conversion uncertainty and material debt. Cash balance is not debt-free liquidity.
next_checks: Reconcile recurring costs versus acquisition/restructuring adjustments
Debt use, dilution and capital allocation
downgrade_conditions: GAAP earnings fail to catch up to adjusted profits
Debt-funded investment fails to earn adequate returns

assessments.thesis: Order intake and Q3 revenue outlook are strong; advanced-packaging demand deserves tracking.
assessments.bear: Recent GAAP profit declined despite revenue growth. Need to separate acquisition/nonrecurring effects from operating deterioration; do not automatically call decline structural.

assessments.thesis: AI wafer-level burn-in orders support a potentially large fiscal 2027 ramp.
assessments.bear: Revenue ramp is still forecast; lead-customer dependence and approximately 20.5x forecast sales at the quoted market cap leave little room for disappointment.
next_checks: Shipments and revenue conversion from announced orders
